newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan convicts Islamist military coup plotters.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan convicts Islamist military coup plotters.

text.p: A Pakistani military court on Wednesday convicted and sentenced four Islamist army officers of plotting a coup against Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government, the Defence Ministry said.

It said in a statement quoted by the official APP news agency that the officers had been found guilty of the charges, including conspiring to overthrow the government by means of criminal force, and were dismissed from the service.

The court sentenced Major General Zahir-ul-Islam Abbasi to seven years in prison, Brigadier Mustansir Billah to 14 years, Colonel Muhammad Azad Minhas to two years and Colonel Inayatullah Khan to four years. The officers may appeal.
They were arrested in September 1995 and tried by a closed court martial in Attock, northwest of Islamabad.

Defence Minister Aftab Shaaban Meerani said last year the plotters had planned to storm a corps commanders' meeting in Rawalpindi on September 30, kill the top officers and take command of the armed forces.

"They had intended to impose a self-styled sharia (Islamic law) and the general officer was to become chief of army staff and 'amirul mu'mineen' (commander of the faithful)," he told the Senate in December.
Pakistani officials said at the time they had seized 26 Kalashnikov assault rifles, a rocket launcher with five rockets, 50 hand grenades and 13 commando uniforms from the plotters.

They had also found written plans, including a draft constitution, the outline of a new political system, a speech to be broadcast on radio and television and lists of people who were to be eliminated or were to be given army posts.
